clue.text: Actor on The Simpsons maybe?

parts.note: surface reading: a performer who appears in the famous American comedy series
setter's reading: the show is an example of the answer, and the answer's second word, set in motion, turns into the first two clue words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a voice performer works on The Simpsons.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a reverse anagram too: make CARTOON ANIMATED, shaking its letters about, and it becomes ACTOR ON. The Simpsons, italicised as a title, is the example being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running American television show about a yellow family is drawn, so it is one example of this kind of programme.

clue.text: Gold to trial TV show — it involves action, but lacks self-awareness

definitions.text: it involves action, but lacks self-awareness

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
a pilot is a trial episode made to test a series

explanation.surface: An acting-heavy TV show launched with a gold budget turns out to be mindless.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is italicised to look like the name of a TV channel, but it is just the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on this setting means carrying out tasks mechanically without conscious thought, like a plane flying itself.

clue.text: Playwright sees nurse following bowel disorder

indicators.note: coming after means being placed later in the string, so the order of the parts is fixed

parts.note: irritable bowel syndrome
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A dramatist visits a nurse after a gut complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian author of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist wrote Hedda Gabler and Peer Gynt, so he is a famous writer of stage plays.

clue.text: A bomb that flew over a hill gets airman

parts.note: taken as written
the V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War, its 1 read as the letter I
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A wartime flying bomb passes over a hill and hits a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-1 or doodlebug was a German flying bomb that hit London; the digit 1 is read as the letter I. 'Over' in a down clue simply means the next piece sits after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a person who flies aircraft, the second being the older military term for a pilot.

clue.text: Manipulates topless teenagers in broadcast without adult

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter at the head of the word is cut off
without means lacking, so the letter standing for a grown-up is taken away
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word minus its first letter and minus the A for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of someone exploiting half-naked teenagers on air with no grown-up present.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters go before the shuffle: the T at the top and the A for adult. What remains of teenagers, plus IN, is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a result is to arrange or contrive it cleverly, a synonym of steering events by stealth.

clue.text: Blame kept out of sight in church

indicators.note: one thing being inside another means it is enclosed by it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Guilt is concealed within a church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword church besides CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or rebuke someone is to find fault with them, close to the verb meaning to hold them responsible.

clue.text: Enlisted revolutionary when I deported some characters

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
only a few of the letters in the following words are wanted, sitting together in a run

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A rebel was conscripted after the speaker was expelled from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is wheN I DEPORted, read right to left. 'Revolutionary' looks like a person but is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone persuaded or recruited to help is said to be brought into a task, like cattle caught with a lasso.

clue.text: Eccentric playing banjo, entertaining millions is jack of all trades

parts.note: odd means strange

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another
playing an instrument works it about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the instrument's letters
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A quirky banjo player pulling in millions turns out to be a man of many skills.
explanation.walkthrough: BANJO rearranges to JOBAN, and M for millions goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman who does small tasks of every kind is a person able to turn a hand to anything.

clue.text: Jog naked around the centre of Margate

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: nude means unclothed

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A naked run through the middle of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is an English seaside resort in Kent. 'Jog' looks like running but means a small push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a gentle push, the same light prod meant here.

clue.text: Troubling quality — ask for husband

indicators.note: one thing given for another is swapped in to replace it

parts.note: a thing can be an attribute or quality
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A worrying character trait: asking for a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take THING and replace its H with ASK: T-ASK-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding, burdensome job is described as taxing or onerous, so it is putting a strain on someone.

clue.text: Independent politician two journalists obstructed

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a Member of Parliament
ED, an editor, twice

explanation.surface: A lone politician was blocked by a pair of reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: ED for editor is the stock crossword journalist; 'two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindered and blocked progress are near synonyms, both meaning something was held back or got in the way.

clue.text: Coppers taking dope and ecstasy show remorse

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the outer piece encloses the others

parts.note: copper coins, pennies
a dope is an idiot, a nit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police caught with drugs are made to look sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' wants to be police and 'dope' a drug; they are pennies and a fool. British copper coins are the penny and two pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow for wrongdoing and repentance are close synonyms, both describing regret felt over a sin.

clue.text: Some cattle rustler finally wearing symbol of peace

indicators.note: whatever is worn is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the dove is the traditional emblem of peace

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so just the closing letter is used

parts.note: the word's closing letter

explanation.surface: A cattle thief ends up wearing a peace badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some cattle' looks like the start of a hidden-word signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd or flock of animals being driven along together is a collective term for a group of livestock.

clue.text: Gun — one found on a slippery slope

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a German semi-automatic pistol

definitions.text: one found on a slippery slope
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone riding a small toboggan down an ice track

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery slope' sounds like a moral warning, but it is a literal icy run; a luge is a racing sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the brand name of a German army pistol and the term for a competitor in the luge event.

clue.text: Irregular glue ear? Dr will clean occasionally

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether an odd case of glue ear will get the doctor's cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like a comment on the ailment but is the definition: irregulars are unofficial fighters. Glue ear is a build-up of fluid in the middle ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular troops are fighters outside a regular army, and this kind of small independent band is the classic example.

clue.text: It's designed with you in mind — for this reason, don't start cryptic

indicators.note: refusing to begin means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
gnomic means cryptic or enigmatic; its G is lost

explanation.surface: A setter tells the solver that this puzzle was made for them, so they should not start being obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden word here is GNOMIC, meaning terse and enigmatic, which loses its silent G.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture and tools shaped for the comfort and efficiency of the human body are made around the person using them.

clue.text: Wordy newspaper reversed rule on use to wipe bottoms

indicators.note: wiping off the bottom of each word removes its last letter
reversed means turned back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
the word less its last letter
the word less its last letter
the word less its last letter

explanation.surface: A long-winded paper overturned its policy on toilet hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms' is plural: the last letter goes from each of rule, on and use.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkative, chattering person uses too many words, so loquacious and verbose are close synonyms.

clue.text: Hundred players in audition with leading agents to make some bread

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: an audition is heard, so what matters is the sound of the words

parts.note: The Hundred is an English cricket competition, and its players include batters; non-rhotic speech drops the R

explanation.surface: Cricketers try out alongside top spies in order to earn some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hundred' is not C here: The Hundred is a 100-ball cricket tournament. 'Bread' teases money, but it is loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat Italian loaves made with olive oil are a type of bread, and the plural fits the quantity phrase.

clue.text: Ideas man is stopping other Queen moving round

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills the inside of another
letters moved about are put into a different order

parts.note: the word's letters
ER is Elizabeth Regina
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker is blocking another monarch who is on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is the usual ER, Elizabeth Regina; 'moving round' shuffles the letters rather than circling anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dreams up hypotheses and abstract explanations is a person who produces concepts rather than practical work.

clue.text: Dodges game

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fast indoor court sport, forerunner of squash

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodges game' reads like ducking in a playground; a dodge is a scheme to cheat, and rackets is a British court sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent schemes are illegal money-making operations, and the sport played with a ball against walls shares that plural name.

clue.text: Henry rejecting Boleyn's hair dye

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: a rejected thing is sent back, so the letters are turned to face the other way

parts.note: Anne Boleyn, second wife of Henry VIII

explanation.surface: Henry VIII turns against Anne Boleyn's colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor surface fits Henry VIII casting off Anne Boleyn, but Henry here is just the unit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The reddish colouring made from a plant's leaves is used to tint hair and decorate skin.

clue.text: Essentially the high priest's a cereal cafe regular?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the middle of three letters

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word's letters

explanation.surface: The chief priest, at heart, is a devotee of a breakfast-cereal café.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cereal Killer Café in east London, serving bowls of cereal, became a byword for trendy hipster culture; 'high priest' is split, not a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend-conscious young person drawn to quirky artisan venues is typical of those who frequented the London cereal bar.

clue.text: Joely Richardson's expressing emotions

indicators.note: the possessive says one name has something within it, so the answer is held inside the letters

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two names

explanation.surface: An actress is being emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across joeLY RIChardson. Joely Richardson is an English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poetry voices the poet's personal feelings, so the adjective describes writing that conveys feeling.

clue.text: Steals seat back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a stool is a seat

explanation.surface: Someone takes the back of a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat back' looks like part of a chair; it is a seat read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunders and pillages are close synonyms of taking goods unlawfully, especially during a riot or war.

clue.text: Papa's Got A Brand New Bag after interruption by posh, London Philharmonic Orchestra player

indicators.note: being interrupted means something breaks into the middle, splitting the string apart

parts.note: P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: something made brand new is remade, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: U means upper-class
its standard initials
the word's letters

explanation.surface: James Brown's song title is performed after some upper-class orchestral musician barges in.
explanation.walkthrough: Papa's Got A Brand New Bag is a James Brown hit; the answer is the French footballer who played for Manchester United, and the U and LPO break into P-A-GBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The French midfielder is a professional footballer, so he is one example of a sportsman on a team.

clue.text: Copy long division — can it raise the power?

indicators.note: a division is a split between words, and the answer straddles that gap

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether copying out long division could make them more powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across coPY LONg. The definition is a question because a pylon lifts power cables rather than generating power.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall steel towers carry high-voltage electricity cables above the ground, lifting the electrical supply into the air.

clue.text: Get government file

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for government
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: An instruction to obtain an official dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' looks like a folder of papers but is the metalworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a point is to understand it, and comprehending an idea is the same sense of mental seizing.

clue.text: It supplies crude painting effectively

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oil paints
done well is done effectively

explanation.surface: Someone provides rough-and-ready artwork efficiently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' seems to describe the painting but it is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore sunk into the ground produces petroleum, the unrefined fuel that is called crude.

clue.text: Reject striking actors

parts.note: workers on strike are out
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn down performers who are on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a person rejected by society.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah shunned by others is someone cast aside, which is the noun sense of a discarded person.

clue.text: Sailor smooths voyage on board ship bearing European flag

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel means being inside it, so the pieces go within

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it along, so one more piece is added to the string

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to sand wood is to smooth it
a trip is a journey
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A seaman tidies up on a ship flying a European ensign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European flag' tempts the solver towards the EU's circle of stars, but European only supplies a letter and the flag is American.
explanation.definitionFit: The national banner of the United States, with its fifty white stars and red and white bands, is a flag.
